singular_truth: mesh-llm splits one model's layers across separate machines over a peer-to-peer mesh (built on iroh, NAT-traversing, no central server) and serves the whole thing as one ordinary OpenAI-compatible endpoint on localhost.
money_thing: a model too big for any single machine runs anyway, its layers held live across other people's machines, behind one localhost endpoint your agent already speaks to.
logline: Watch one prompt travel through a model that lives on many machines at once and come back as a single answer.
rejected_default: The obvious treatment for a distributed-inference project is a node-diagram of a mesh plus a terminal typing the install command. Rejected: a static node graph makes the mesh look like an architecture slide, and a terminal demo of `mesh-llm serve` shows a command, not the ONE cool thing (a model living across machines). The singular truth is a JOURNEY -- a prompt flowing through layers on different peers -- so a continuous-camera oner that travels through the distributed pipeline shows it far better than a diagram, and it is a device the last dozen videos have not used.
references: a single unbroken Steadicam oner (Children of Men corridor) as the camera-through-the-system idea
network telemetry / distributed-systems dashboards for the peers-connecting beat
mesh-llm's own near-black + electric-blue site identity
